title: open_with picks the integer width by text length and ignores the header's int_size
body:
`SuffixArray::open_with` (`libsufr/src/lib.rs`, around line 95) picks the integer width by text length: `read_text_length` under `u32::MAX` opens as `TypedSuffixArray<u32>`, otherwise `<u64>`. The file records its width in `Header::int_size` and the open path ignores it. A text under 4 GiB written as u64 opens as u32 and is misread.

The only way to write such a file is `SuffixArrayBuilder::with_force_64bit` (`build.rs:154`), which is `pub(crate)` under `cfg(test)` because of the above: only `TypedSuffixArray::<u64>::open` can read what it writes. The unit test at `lib.rs:270` uses that path. Both came in with the commit that restored the builder API from dev.

The construction oracle (sufr-a88738) is an integration test and so cannot build or open a u64 file. It covers u32 only until this is fixed.

## Proposal

- `open_with` reads the header and dispatches on `int_size`.
- `with_force_64bit` becomes a public builder setting, without `cfg(test)`.
- The oracle's table then runs every row at both widths.
close_reason: Not a bug: the format records no width, and open_with applies the format's rule, 4 bytes under u32::MAX of text. Whether the header should record the width is sufr-fde85d; what becomes of with_force_64bit is sufr-11e453. Closed by Jack on 2026-11-03.
